chunks: Ibn Hajar said in Lisan al-Mizan, vol. 5, p. 368:

(Scholar of the Rafida, author of heretical works — being two hundred compositions in which he criticized the Salaf; he wielded great power due to 'Adud al-Dawla; eighty thousand Rafidis accompanied his funeral procession; he died in the year 413)
Then he mentioned the saying of al-Khatib:

(He was greatly given to asceticism, reverence, and devotion to knowledge; a group of scholars graduated through his tutelage, and he excelled in the Imami doctrinal school to the point that it was said: 'he has a favor upon every Imam'; his father was a teacher in Wasit and he was born there; he was killed in 'Ukbara; and it is said that 'Adud al-Dawla would visit him at his home and would visit him when he was ill)

key_terms.الإِكْبَابِ: devoted, single-minded immersion and absorption (in a pursuit)
key_terms.الرَّافِضَةِ: al-Rafida — polemical Sunni designation for Shia Muslims
key_terms.الْبِدْعِيَّةِ: heretical, innovated — applied by Ibn Hajar to al-Mufid's works from a hostile Sunni perspective
key_terms.مِنَّةٌ: favor, benefaction, service rendered deserving gratitude

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani record about Sheikh al-Mufid in Lisan al-Mizan, and what praise did al-Khatib al-Baghdadi bestow upon him?
ai.summary: This passage records Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's entry on Sheikh al-Mufid (d. 413 AH) in Lisan al-Mizan (vol. 5, p. 368), describing him from a polemical Sunni viewpoint as the preeminent authority of the Rafida and author of two hundred works criticising the early Muslim community, wielding enormous influence under the Buyid ruler 'Adud al-Dawla. Ibn Hajar then cites al-Khatib al-Baghdadi's more nuanced account, which praises al-Mufid's profound asceticism, single-minded devotion to scholarship, and unrivalled mastery of Imami doctrine — to the point that it was said: 'he has a favor upon every Imam.'
